name: Example: Using Properties of Midpoints to Calculate an Unknown Value From a Diagram
problem:
Given that $M$ is the midpoint of $\overline{PQ}$, what is the value of $x?$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14171842/assets/bf08731ef8b88b55c1b3df41e58443beefb5e1a69b46757fbfb18c22d6c0b6b1.png)
worked_solution:
Since $M$ is the midpoint of $\overline{PQ}$, the segment $\overline{PQ}$ is twice the length of the segment $\overline{PM}.$ So, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}2PM & =PQ \\ 2(4x-3) & =5x+9 \\ 8x-6 & =5x+9\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we subtract $5x$ from both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}8x-6-5x & =5x+9-5x \\ 3x-6 & =9\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we add $6$ to both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}3x-6+6 & =9+6 \\ 3x & =15\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we divide both sides by $3{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3x}{3} & =\frac{15}{3} \\ x & =5\end{aligned}
$$
